summary.body:
Five signals this week converge on a single thesis: AI's market structure is shifting from subsidized experimentation to enterprise infrastructure billing, and Krish's ventures sit at the inflection point. The trigger is unmistakable — Anthropic, Google, and Meta are blocking third-party AI subscriptions because autonomous agents are crushing their infrastructure. Claude Pro at $20 costs $200-400 in compute. Microsoft lost $80 per user on Copilot. The consumer-subsidy era is ending, and the vendors are sprinting toward IPO-ready unit economics. This is not a threat. This is the moment AI cost governance becomes a board-level line item, and MindMaker is positioned to be the partner CFOs call when the surprise bills land.

Simultaneously, AI development is maturing from 'vibe coding' to structured engineering. GitHub's Spec Kit hit 100k stars with 206 contributors and 30+ agent integrations — under an MIT license no less — signaling that the industry knows ad-hoc code generation creates fragility that compounds in weeks, not months. Keith Shields at Designli put it bluntly: vibe coders are roughly two weeks from discovering their technical debt. The engineering governance market is forming in real time. Non-technical founders who shipped fast with AI now need audits, architecture reviews, and maturity frameworks. This is Felix's lane and the window is wide open.

Anthropic's Claude for Small Business — 15 pre-built workflows with QuickBooks, PayPal, HubSpot, Canva, DocuSign, Google Workspace, and Microsoft 365 — compresses the easy consulting wedge. Basic automation and simple integrations are now commodities. This is bullish, not bearish. It forces consultants upmarket into verticals, messy integrations, and regulatory complexity where defensible value lives. The bottom-feeders get cleared out. MindMaker's consulting tier gets a cleaner competitive field and a sharper value proposition by necessity.

The macro picture: AI pricing is transitioning from SaaS seat models to infrastructure usage models. AI coding is transitioning from ad-hoc generation to auditable workflows. AI consulting is transitioning from general tools to vertical solutions. Every one of these transitions creates a governance gap, and governance gaps are where premium advisory revenue lives. Krish has clear runway to build the cost audit offering, the engineering maturity service, and the regulated-industry consulting packages before the market widely recognizes these openings.

top_3_actions.action: Launch AI cost audit and predictive budgeting service for finance teams facing vendor price transitions
Build engineering governance maturity framework for non-technical founders who shipped with vibe coding
Package vertical-specific consulting for regulated industries as the Claude SMB launch commoditizes basic automation

summary.blockers: No blockers. Krish has clear runway. The market signals are tailwinds, not headwinds.
